title: Working at Redwood: Roles, Career Ladders, Benefits, Hiring & Onboarding, and Internal Tools
author: Aisha Patel
content:
Overview

This page consolidates core policies and guidance for employees joining and growing at Redwood Inference. It covers: roles and career ladders, benefits and perks overview, hiring and onboarding process, and essential internal tools and how to access them. Use this as the canonical reference for people-ops and managers; operational checklists and team-specific supplements are linked in Related pages.

1) Working at Redwood — high level

Intro: Redwood is an engineering-first company focused on production LLM inference. We prioritize clear expectations, measurable outcomes, and career development. This section summarizes our culture, values, and practical advice for new and existing employees.

- Our values: ownership, reliability, curiosity, customer empathy, and technical excellence.
- Work model: hybrid-first; each team publishes a team-level remote/hybrid policy in team wiki.
- Hours & flexible time: core overlap 10:00–15:00 local team timezone; flexible start/finish otherwise.

A. New hire first 30/90 days (manager + new hire checklist):

1. Before start (People Ops): onboarding packet, hardware order, pre-boarding docs.
2. Day 1: Welcome call, HR benefit enrollment walkthrough, account provisioning (email, SSO, Slack, Jira, Confluence).
3. Week 1: Team orientation, codebase walkthrough, first 1:1 scheduled with manager, onboarding buddy assigned.
4. 30-day check-in: expectations review, initial project assignment.
5. 90-day review: performance calibration (informal), feedback collection, career conversation.

Checklist (manager actions):
- Create onboarding plan in Confluence with milestones and deliverables.
- Ensure dev environment and access are functional by Day 3.
- Assign onboarding tasks and review schedule.

2) Roles and career ladders

Summary: Redwood uses role-based career ladders per functional area. Ladders define scope, impact, competencies, and promotion criteria. All ladders live in team wikis and are derived from the company-level framework below.

Company-level framework (high-level):
- Individual Contributor (IC): IC1 (entry), IC2 (experienced), IC3 (senior), IC4 (staff), IC5 (principal).
- Managerial: Mgr1 (first-line), Mgr2 (senior manager), Dir (director), VP (vice president).

Key dimensions evaluated for promotion:
- Technical mastery and execution (quality, reliability, measurable outcomes).
- Scope & influence (code, systems, people).
- Leadership and mentorship (guidance, hiring, coaching).
- Product & customer impact (understanding business needs, driving outcomes).

Promotion process (summary):
1. Prepare a promotion packet: goals achieved, measurable impact, peer/manager feedback, examples of work.
2. Manager endorsement and calibration with peer managers.
3. Promotion committee review (biweekly) with cross-functional stakeholders.
4. HR & compensation finalize level and compensation changes.

Examples of expectations by role (brief):
- IC2 (Experienced Engineer): Owns components, delivers features with minimal guidance, participates in code reviews, reliable on-call contributor.
- IC3 (Senior Engineer): Leads significant features, influences architecture, mentors junior engineers, drives quality & performance improvements.
- Staff/Principal: Cross-team technical leadership, significant product or platform ownership, shapes roadmap and standards.

3) Benefits & perks (summary and enrollment)

Core benefits (US & select regions — check regional People Ops pages for local variations):
- Medical, dental, vision plans with employer contribution.
- 401(k) with company match (US).
- Parental leave: 16 weeks primary, 8 weeks secondary (paid), plus flexible return-to-work options.
- Generous paid time off: 20 days PTO + company holidays and discretionary wellness days.
- Flexible spending accounts, commuter benefits (where applicable).
- Equity grants and annual refresh eligibility per role level.

Perks:
- Stipend for home office and co-working, plus monthly learning stipend.
- Wellness reimbursement and mental health support via EAP.
- Company retreats (annual), team off-sites (budgeted per team).
- Internal learning programs and technical study groups.

Enrollment & changes:
- New hires must enroll in benefits within 30 days of start date.
- Changes outside open enrollment require a qualifying life event; contact People Ops for forms.

4) Hiring & interview process (overview for hiring managers and candidates)

Principles: fast, equitable, and transparent. Our goal is to balance candidate experience with rigorous assessment for role fit and potential.

Standard process (software engineering example):
1. Requisition approved and posted by Recruiting.
2. Phone screen (30–45m) — hiring manager or recruiter screens for role fit and basic technical competence.
3. Technical screen (coding/system design; 60m) — pair-programming or take-home assignment depending on level.
4. Onsite loop (virtual/in-person) — 3–5 interviews including hiring manager, peer ladder interviews, and a leadership conversation as appropriate.
5. Debrief and hire/no-hire decision within 72 hours.
6. Offer issued and negotiation support from Recruiting.

Fair hiring checkpoints:
- Diverse interview panel where possible.
- Standardized rubrics per role and level (questions & evaluation forms in Recruiting toolkit).
- Reasonable accommodations on request.

Candidate experience tips (for interviewers):
- Share concrete context and expectations for the role.
- Provide timely feedback; adhere to scheduled commitments.
- Avoid unnecessary proprietary or NDA-covered content during interviews.

5) Onboarding & first 90-day programs (detailed resources)

Programs:
- New Hire Orientation (weekly cohort): Benefits walkthrough, IT provisioning, security training, company values and product overview.
- Engineering onboarding: codebase tours, architecture overview sessions, runtime and infra deep dives.
- Manager onboarding: people management workshops, performance cycles, compensation training.

Templates and required training (links in team wiki):
- Onboarding plan template (Confluence).
- First-90-day goal template (OKR-style).
- Mandatory security & compliance training (complete by Day 14).
- Privacy & data handling training (complete by Day 30 for product-facing roles).

6) Internal tools and access guide

Core tools and access flows (quick reference):
- SSO / Identity: Okta — primary authentication for company accounts. Provisioning: People Ops + IT.
- Communication: Slack — public channels, team channels, on-call channels; naming conventions: team-<name>, proj-<name>, oncall-<service>.
- Docs & knowledge: Confluence — canonical docs, team pages, runbooks. Use page templates for runbooks and PRDs.
- Code hosting: GitHub Enterprise — repo naming: infra/*, runtime/*, services/*; use protected branches and CI checks.
- CI/CD: GitHub Actions + internal runners; deployment approvals use GitHub PRs + Ops review for production.
- Issue tracking: Jira — project keys per team; triage board maintained by engineering managers.
- Observability & alerts: Datadog for metrics/traces, Sentry for errors, PagerDuty for on-call routing.
- Secrets & keys: HashiCorp Vault / KMS integrations for keys; use restricted access and rotate keys per policy.
- HR & payroll: Workday / Rippling for payroll, PTO, and benefits enrollment (depending on region).

Access request flow (standard):
1. New hire access is provisioned by People Ops + IT (Okta group assignments).
2. For additional resource access (repos, cloud accounts), open an access request in the Access & Permissions template in Confluence; approver is typically your manager and the service owner.
3. For urgent access, escalate to IT Slack #it-ops and tag People Ops.

Security & compliance reminders:
- MFA required for all accounts.
- Do not store production secrets in personal machines; use approved secret stores.
- Follow least privilege when requesting roles.

7) Manager responsibilities & best practices

Hiring & onboarding: timely interview feedback, structured offers, candidate debriefs.
People growth: conduct regular 1:1s, career conversations, and document performance/feedback.
Operational ownership: ensure on-call rotation coverage, runbook ownership, and incident postmortems.

8) Additional resources and how to use this page

- Use the Related pages links for team-specific variants, benefits policy details, and region-specific legal pages.
- To propose changes to this page, file a Confluence edit and add People Ops as reviewer; substantial changes (policy or benefits) require People Ops + Legal review.
